results.name: Cable Silverback Shrug
instructions: Stand facing a low cable pulley while holding a straight bar with both hands at shoulder width apart, using an overhand grip. Hinge slightly at your hips and keep your arms fully extended.
Elevate your shoulders toward your ears while keeping your elbows straight and your torso still.
Pause briefly at the top while squeezing your upper back muscles.
Lower your shoulders slowly to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your arms fully extended throughout the exercise.
Maintain a slight hip hinge and a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Squeeze your upper trapezius at the top of each repetition.
Inhale as you lower your shoulders and exhale as you shrug upward.
results.description: Cable Silverback Shrug is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Shoulders, Core.

results.name: Chin Up Reverse Close Grip
instructions: Begin by grasping a pull-up bar with a close underhand grip (palms facing you) and your hands placed closer than shoulder-width apart. Hang with your arms fully extended and your legs slightly bent or crossed behind you.
Engage your back and start pulling your body upward by bending your elbows and contracting your biceps, continuing until your chin is above the bar.
Lower yourself back to the starting position with a controlled movement, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your biceps and upper back muscles to lift your body, avoiding excessive momentum.
Perform the movement slowly and with control, especially during the lowering phase, to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you pull up and inhaling as you lower yourself.
Use a full range of motion by fully extending your arms at the bottom and bringing your chin above the bar at the top.
results.description: Chin Up Reverse Close Grip is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Chin Up Reverse Normal Grip
instructions: Begin by grasping a pull-up bar with an underhand grip (palms facing you) and your hands shoulder-width apart. Hang with your arms fully extended and your legs slightly bent or crossed behind you.
Engage your core and pull your shoulder blades down and back to start the movement.
Pull your body upward by bending your elbows and contracting your biceps, continuing until your chin is above the bar.
Lower yourself back to the starting position with a controlled movement, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your biceps and back muscles to lift your body, avoiding excessive momentum.
Perform the movement slowly and with control, especially during the lowering phase, to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you pull up and inhaling as you lower yourself.
Use a full range of motion by fully extending your arms at the bottom and bringing your chin above the bar at the top.
results.description: Chin Up Reverse Normal Grip is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

Pull your body upward by bending your elbows and contracting your biceps, continuing until your chin is above the bar.

results.name: Dumbbell Alternating Pendlay Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand. Bend your knees and hinge forward at your hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, allowing both arms to hang straight beneath your shoulders, resting the dumbbells on the floor.
Pull one dumbbell toward your abdomen by driving your elbow upward close to your body, while keeping the opposite arm extended.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control until your arm is fully extended.
Repeat the movement with the opposite arm, alternating sides while maintaining the bent-over position throughout the exercise.
tips: Keep your back flat and your chest facing the floor throughout the movement.
Brace your core to prevent your torso from rotating as you row.
Maintain a neutral neck by looking toward the floor a few feet in front of you.
Inhale as you lower the dumbbell and exhale as you pull it upward.
results.description: Dumbbell Alternating Pendlay Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders, Core.

results.name: Dumbbell Goblet Good Morning
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell vertically against your chest with both hands. Keep your knees slightly bent and your core engaged.
Push your hips back and hinge your torso forward while keeping the dumbbell close to your chest and your back straight.
Lower your torso until it is nearly parallel to the floor or until you feel a comfortable stretch in your hamstrings.
Drive your hips forward to return to the upright position, then repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Push your hips backward instead of bending forward through your waist.
Keep your spine neutral and avoid rounding your lower back.
Keep your weight balanced over the middle of your feet and heels.
Inhale as you hinge forward and exhale as you return to standing.
results.description: Dumbbell Goblet Good Morning is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Upper Back, Biceps.

results.name: Dumbbell Knee Lawnmower Row
instructions: Begin in a wide stance with one foot pointing forward and the other pointing to the side. Bend your knees, lean forward, brace your free hand on your thigh, and hold the dumbbell between your legs with an overhand grip.
Pull the dumbbell toward your abdomen while keeping your torso still, rotating your hand from an overhand grip to an underhand grip as your elbow moves upward and backward.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your back muscles while keeping your hips and shoulders steady.
Lower the dumbbell with control while rotating your hand back to an overhand grip, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Keep your torso still without twisting as you lift the dumbbell.
Pull the dumbbell toward your abdomen while keeping your elbow close to your body.
Keep your working shoulder down and avoid shrugging as you row.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbell upward and inhale as you lower it.
results.description: Dumbbell Knee Lawnmower Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Core.

results.name: Dumbbell Pendlay Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand using a neutral grip. Bend your knees and hinge forward until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, with the dumbbells hanging below your shoulders.
Brace your core and pull both dumbbells toward your abdomen by driving your elbows upward and backward close to your body.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your back muscles while keeping your torso fixed.
Lower both dumbbells with control until your arms are fully extended and the dumbbells touch the floor. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and your torso nearly parallel to the floor.
Pull the dumbbells toward your abdomen rather than toward your chest.
Keep your torso still and avoid using momentum to lift the weights.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbells upward and inhale as you lower them.
results.description: Dumbbell Pendlay Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms, Lower Back.

results.name: Dumbbell Bent Over Row (Pronated Grip)
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips. Let your arms hang straight down from your shoulders.
Pull the dumbbells towards your hips, keeping your elbows close to your body and squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Hold the contraction for a moment, focusing on engaging your back muscles.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your shoulders.
Exhale as you pull the dumbbells up and inhale as you lower them.
Focus on pulling with your back muscles rather than your arms.
results.description: Dumbbell Bent Over Row (Pronated Grip) is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders.
